question: An operations manager is preparing to let her team use Claude-drafted replies across a busy customer queue. She has not yet decided who checks what. What should she do first?
options: A) Send the replies out and collect complaints, so the team learns which cases were handled badly.
B) Ask Claude to mark the replies it is least certain about so those can be routed for checking.
C) Have every reply read by two colleagues, so that nothing can reach a customer unchecked at all.
D) Agree what a good reply looks like and which mistakes would actually be costly to the business.
correct_answers: D) Agree what a good reply looks like and which mistakes would actually be costly to the business.
explanations: Incorrect. Learning from customer complaints puts the cost of the error onto customers, which is the outcome a review step exists to prevent.
Incorrect. A self-reported certainty score is produced by the same process as the reply, so it is not a dependable basis for routing work to a reviewer.
Incorrect. Double-reading everything is expensive and unfocused, and it is a decision about process taken before anyone has defined what reviewers are looking for.
Correct. Review only works against a standard. Naming what a correct reply contains and which failures would hurt is what tells the team where scrutiny is needed and where it is not.
